cards.text: Grab an apron, friend, because today the crowns come off FAST. God's people are split into two kingdoms: Israel in the north and Judah in the south (1 Kings 12:16-20). In the fifteenth year of Amaziah king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash becomes king of Israel, and he reigns in Samaria forty-one years.

cards.question: Same name, different man. Israel's first king, Jeroboam son of Nebat, led Israel into sin with golden calves (1 Kings 12:28-30). What does this new King Jeroboam do about those sins?

answers.text: He doesn't turn away from them
He tears down all of them
He makes Israel repent of them

cards.text: Yep. He does evil in the sight of the LORD. And yet, PLOT TWIST: this Jeroboam wins back Israel's borders, from Lebo-hamath all the way to the Sea of the Arabah.

cards.question: The LORD had said those borders would come back, through His servant the prophet. And this prophet has a famous fish story of his own. Who is it?

cards.text: YES. THAT Jonah, son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher (Jonah 1:1). Friend, I spent years stuck in a junk drawer, and this man got swallowed by a great fish (Jonah 1:17) and STILL came out with a steady prophet job.
So why does the LORD do this for Israel? He sees that their suffering is very bitter, slave and free, and there's no one to help Israel.

cards.question: The LORD also had said something about Israel's future. What had He said He would not do to Israel?

answers.text: Blot out its name from under heaven
Give its land to the king of Assyria
Leave it without a single prophet

cards.question: The LORD saves Israel by the hand of Jeroboam son of Jehoash, the same king who does evil in His sight.

cards.text: Jeroboam even recovers Damascus and Hamath for Israel. Then he rests with his fathers, and his son Zechariah reigns in his place.
Down south in Judah, in Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year, Azariah son of Amaziah becomes king at SIXTEEN years old. Friend, I've got oven mitts older than that.

cards.question: Sixteen-year-old Azariah goes on to reign in Jerusalem for ___ years.
King Azariah of Judah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.

cards.text: FIFTY-TWO YEARS on the throne, and he walks it right. But you KNOW there's a but: the high places are not taken away.

cards.question: During Azariah's reign, what do the people keep doing at the high places?

cards.text: Then the LORD afflicts King Azariah with leprosy, and he has it until the day he dies.

cards.question: With King Azariah sick with leprosy, who takes charge of the palace and governs the people of the land?
With leprosy, King Azariah lives in a separate ___.

cards.text: The rest of Azariah's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Then he rests with his fathers in the City of David, and his son Jotham reigns in his place.
Back up north. In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's reign over Judah, Jeroboam's son Zechariah becomes king of Israel in Samaria.

cards.question: Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel in Samaria for six years.

cards.text: Six MONTHS, friend. He does evil as his fathers had done, and then Shallum son of Jabesh conspires against him.

cards.question: How does Shallum's conspiracy against King Zechariah end?

answers.text: He kills Zechariah in front of the people
He drives Zechariah out of Samaria
He makes Zechariah give up the throne

cards.text: Then the passage points out that a word the LORD spoke to Jehu, an earlier king of Israel, has come true. Jehu's line on the throne went Jehu, then Jehoahaz, then Jehoash, then Jeroboam, then Zechariah (2 Kings 10:35; 13:9; 14:16, 29).

cards.question: So how many generations of Jehu's sons had the LORD said would sit on the throne of Israel?

cards.text: Shallum becomes king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah's reign over Judah. Uzziah is just another name for Azariah, same king (2 Kings 15:7, 32).

cards.question: Shallum son of Jabesh reigns in Samaria one full ___.

cards.text: ONE MONTH. Friend, I've had dust sit on me in that junk drawer longer than this man sat on a throne. Then Menahem son of Gadi comes up from Tirzah to Samaria.

cards.question: Menahem son of Gadi strikes down and kills Shallum, and reigns in his place.

cards.text: Then Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacks the town of Tiphsah and everyone around it.

cards.question: Why does Menahem attack Tiphsah?

answers.text: They would not open their gates
They had sided with the king of Judah

cards.text: No joke here, friend. The attack is brutal: Menahem rips open all the pregnant women.
Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria, and through his whole reign he doesn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. Then Pul king of Assyria invades the land.

cards.question: When Pul king of Assyria invades, Menahem hands him a thousand talents of ___.
Menahem pays Pul to gain his support and strengthen his own grip on the kingdom.
A thousand talents is a LOT of silver. Who does Menahem collect it from?
Once Menahem pays the silver, what does the king of Assyria do?

cards.text: Fifty shekels of silver from every wealthy man. That's the group chat NOBODY wants to get added to. Then Menahem rests with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah reigns in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah's reign over Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem becomes king of Israel. He reigns two years in Samaria, and he does evil in the sight of the LORD.

cards.question: Then one of King Pekahiah's own officers conspires against him. Who is it?

cards.text: Pekah, with Argob, Arieh and fifty men of Gilead, strikes down Pekahiah at the citadel of the king's palace and reigns in his place. Pekah takes the throne from PEKAHIAH. Friend, I read that three times and I'm STILL checking who's who.

cards.question: Pekah son of Remaliah reigns over Israel in Samaria for ___ years.

cards.text: In Pekah's days, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes. He captures a whole list of towns, plus Gilead, Galilee and all the land of Naphtali.

cards.question: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria leaves the people he captures in their own land.
Then Hoshea son of Elah leads a conspiracy against King Pekah. What does Hoshea do?

cards.text: Zechariah? Killed. Shallum? Killed. Pekahiah? Killed. Pekah? KILLED. Friend, at this point I'm not sure I'd want that chair.
Down south in Judah, in the second year of Pekah's reign, Jotham son of Uzziah becomes king. He's twenty-five, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem.

cards.question: How does King Jotham of Judah do in the eyes of the LORD?

answers.text: Right just like his father Uzziah
Evil just like the kings of Israel
Right at first and evil later

cards.text: And yes, the high places still aren't taken away. But Jotham does build something at the house of the LORD.

cards.question: King Jotham rebuilds the Upper ___ of the house of the LORD.
In Jotham's days, trouble starts heading for Judah. Which two kings does the LORD begin to send against Judah?

cards.text: Jotham rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David, and his son Ahaz reigns in his place. Friend, that is a WHOLE lot of crowns for one batch.

findings.problem: The question calls Jeroboam son of Nebat "Israel's first king." Saul was Israel's first king (1 Samuel 10). Jeroboam son of Nebat was the first king of the northern kingdom after the split. Something like "the first king of the northern kingdom" would be accurate.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The hint calls Jonah's account "a famous fish story." In everyday English, a "fish story" means an exaggerated or made-up tale, so the humor lands on Scripture's account itself.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The joke says Jonah was swallowed by the fish and "STILL came out with a steady prophet job." That claims the fish came before his word about Jeroboam's borders. Neither 2 Kings 14:25 nor Jonah gives that order. The card also puts "(Jonah 1:1)" right after "the prophet from Gath-hepher," but Gath-hepher appears only in 2 Kings 14:25, not Jonah 1:1.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The punchline "I've got oven mitts older than that" is a joke about Azariah's age.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.

findings.problem: The story card has three full sentences. The group chat comparison also doesn't share the core action, which is being made to pay fifty shekels each. It doesn't click without explaining.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Joke logic: "the group chat NOBODY wants to get added to" doesn't match the action of being made to hand over silver, and a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card has three full sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says Hoshea "leads a conspiracy against King Pekah," and that rules out the wrong answer "Makes peace with him."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card is a recap of the four kings already shown killed (15:10, 14, 25, 30). It tells no new part of the passage. It also runs well past 1 to 2 sentences, in fragments.
The card says Jotham "does build something." The text says he "rebuilt" the Upper Gate (15:35).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Cards 7 and 8 have just stressed that Pekah was killed ("Pekah? KILLED."). A thoughtful baker would reason that Pekah can't be sent against Judah and would rule out the right answer. The story cards never set up that 15:37 looks back to Jotham's days, while Pekah was still alive, and Rezin is never introduced.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Pekah's verdict in 15:28 (he did evil and did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat) is never told. Every other king's verdict is covered, and the verdict is the backbone of this passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Many choice cards are pure discovery details the baker can't reason out: reign lengths and numbers (S1 C11 fifty-two, S2 C2 six years vs months, S2 C8 month, S3 C4 twenty), small details (S1 C17 house, S2 C15 silver, S3 C12 Gate), and 50/50 statements copied from unseen verses (S1 C12, S2 C16). That is more than "a few," and several are details that don't move the passage forward.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
